original: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.
simplified: An agreement becomes a valid contract when: 1) Parties agree freely, 2) Parties are legally capable, 3) There is lawful purpose and consideration, 4) Not declared void by law.
meaning: Defines essential elements of a valid contract in Indian law.

original: When one person signifies to another his willingness to do or to abstain from doing anything, with a view to obtaining the assent of that other to such act or abstinence, he is said to make a proposal.
simplified: A proposal (offer) is made when someone shows willingness to do or not do something, wanting the other persons agreement.
meaning: Defines what constitutes a legal offer or proposal.

original: A contract may be avoided if it is caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake.
simplified: A contract can be cancelled if it was made under pressure, influence, deception, false statements, or errors.
meaning: Lists situations where a contract can be voided due to invalid consent.

original: When, at the desire of the promisor, the promisee or any other person has done or abstained from doing, or does or abstains from doing, or promises to do or to abstain from doing, something, such act or abstinence or promise is called a consideration for the promise.
simplified: Consideration means something in return - when someone does something because the other person asked for it, that something is called consideration.

original: An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void.
simplified: A void agreement is not legally binding and cannot be enforced in court.

original: An agreement enforceable by law is a contract.
simplified: A contract is a legally binding agreement that can be enforced in court.

original: All contracts are agreements but all agreements are not contracts.
simplified: While every contract is an agreement, not every agreement qualifies as a legally enforceable contract.

original: When a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract.
simplified: If one party refuses to fulfill their contract promise, the other party can cancel the entire contract.
meaning: Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly

original: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
simplified: If a contract is broken, the affected party can claim compensation for any losses suffered.
meaning: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract

original: A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.
simplified: A contract becomes void if it becomes impossible or illegal to perform after the contract is made.

original: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of murder.
simplified: Causing death with intent to kill or cause serious injury amounts to murder.

original: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Murder is punishable with death sentence or life imprisonment, plus possible fine.

original: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
simplified: Dishonestly taking movable property without owner's consent constitutes theft.

original: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Theft is punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both.

original: Whoever causes the death of a person by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits culpable homicide.
simplified: Causing death with intent or knowledge amounts to culpable homicide.

original: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years.
simplified: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder is punishable with life or up to 10 years.
meaning: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder

original: Whoever enters into or upon property in possession of another with intent to commit an offence, is said to commit criminal trespass.
simplified: Entering property with intent to commit offense is criminal trespass.

original: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Criminal trespass is punishable with up to 3 months imprisonment or fine.

original: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished.
simplified: Using force against woman with intent to outrage modesty is punishable.
meaning: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty

original: Whoever, being a husband or relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished.
simplified: Husband or relatives subjecting woman to cruelty can be punished.
meaning: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty

original: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
simplified: Every person has equal rights under the law in India.

original: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression.
simplified: Citizens have right to free speech and expression.

original: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
simplified: No one can be denied life or personal freedom except through legal procedures.
meaning: Protection of life and personal liberty

original: A lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent, can be made only by a registered instrument.
simplified: Long-term leases (over 1 year) must be registered documents.

original: A mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced.
simplified: Mortgage means transferring property interest as security for loan.

original: A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage.
simplified: Hindu marriage requires that neither party has a living spouse at marriage time.

original: Any marriage solemnized, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, may be annulled by a decree of nullity on the ground that the marriage has not been consummated owing to the impotence of the respondent.
simplified: Marriage can be annulled if not consummated due to impotence.

original: Any marriage solemnized may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the ground that the other party has had voluntary sexual intercourse with any person other than his or her spouse.
simplified: Divorce can be granted if spouse has extramarital relations.

original: The Court may issue a commission for the examination on interrogatories or otherwise of any person resident within the local limits of its jurisdiction.
simplified: Court can appoint commissioner to record evidence of witnesses.

original: The Court shall have power to grant a temporary injunction to restrain such act.
simplified: Courts can issue temporary orders to prevent illegal actions.
meaning: Cases in which temporary injunction may be granted

original: No appeal shall lie from a decree passed by the Court with the consent of parties.
simplified: No appeal against judgments where both parties agreed.

original: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who has been concerned in any cognizable offence.
simplified: Police can arrest without warrant anyone involved in serious crimes.
meaning: When police may arrest without warrant

original: In every trial the evidence of each witness shall be recorded in the presence of the accused.
simplified: Witness evidence must be recorded in presence of accused person.
meaning: Evidence to be taken in presence of accused

original: Whenever a person is arrested and detained in custody, it shall be the duty of the person having the custody to take reasonable care of the health and safety of the arrested person.
simplified: Police must take reasonable care of health of arrested persons.
meaning: Health and safety of arrested person

original: A consumer means any person who buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised.
simplified: Consumer is anyone who buys goods or uses services for payment.

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such product.
simplified: Manufacturers responsible for compensating consumers for defective products.

original: Whoever with the intent to cause or knowing that he is likely to cause wrongful loss or damage to the public or any person destroys or deletes or alters any information residing in a computer resource, commits hacking.
simplified: Unauthorized alteration or deletion of computer information is hacking.

original: Where any person without permission accesses or secures access to such computer, he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation.
simplified: Unauthorized computer access can result in compensation payments.
meaning: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.

original: Every company shall have a registered office within fifteen days of its incorporation.
simplified: Every company must have registered office within 15 days of incorporation.

original: Every company shall hold its first annual general meeting within a period of nine months from the date of closing of the first financial year.
simplified: First company meeting must be held within 9 months of financial year end.

original: A negotiable instrument means a promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable either to order or to bearer.
simplified: Negotiable instruments include promissory notes, bills, and cheques.

original: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount is returned by the bank unpaid, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence.
simplified: Bouncing of cheque for payment is a criminal offense.
meaning: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account

original: Notwithstanding that an arbitration agreement is in writing, it shall be deemed to be in writing if it is contained in a document signed by the parties.
simplified: Arbitration agreement can be in written form through signed documents.

original: A party may raise a plea that the arbitral tribunal does not have jurisdiction.
simplified: Objection to arbitrator's jurisdiction must be raised early.
meaning: Competence of arbitral tribunal to rule on its jurisdiction

original: Subject to the provisions of this Act, all citizens shall have the right to information.
simplified: All Indian citizens have right to seek information from public authorities.

original: It shall be the duty of the Public Information Officer to provide information to persons requesting for the information.
simplified: Public Information Officer must provide information to applicants.

original: No person carrying on any industry, operation or process shall discharge or emit any environmental pollutant in excess of such standards as may be prescribed.
simplified: Industries cannot release pollutants beyond prescribed limits.
meaning: Persons carrying on industry, operation, etc., not to allow emission or discharge of environmental pollutants in excess of the standards

original: Whoever fails to comply with any of the provisions of this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine.
simplified: Violating environmental laws can lead to 5 years imprisonment or fine.
meaning: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act and the rules, orders and directions

original: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him authorising him to drive the vehicle.
simplified: Driving without valid license in public places is illegal.

original: Whoever drives a motor vehicle in any public place without holding an effective driving licence shall be punishable.
simplified: Driving without license is punishable.

law_type: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
original: Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years.
simplified: Penetrative sexual assault on child carries minimum 10 years imprisonment.

law_type: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
original: Whoever uses a child for pornographic purposes shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Using children for pornography can lead to 5 years imprisonment and fine.
meaning: Punishment for using child for pornographic purposes

original: Whoever, being a public servant, accepts or obtains any gratification other than legal remuneration, shall be punishable.
simplified: Public servants taking bribes can be punished.
meaning: Public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official act

original: Whoever abets any offence punishable under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years.
simplified: Helping corruption offenses is punishable with 3+ years imprisonment.

original: The property of a male Hindu dying intestate shall devolve according to the provisions of this Chapter.
simplified: Property of Hindu male without will follows specific inheritance rules.
meaning: General rules of succession in the case of males

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 6, the daughter of a coparcener shall by birth become a coparcener in her own right in the same manner as the son.
simplified: Daughter has equal birth rights as son in ancestral property.
meaning: Devolution of interest in coparcenary property

original: The court may grant injunction to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favour of the applicant.
simplified: Court can order injunction to prevent violation of legal obligations.

original: Evidence may be given in any suit or proceeding of the existence or non-existence of every fact in issue and of such other facts as are hereinafter declared to be relevant.
simplified: Evidence can only be given about facts directly relevant to the case.
meaning: Evidence may be given of facts in issue and relevant facts

original: No fact of which the court will take judicial notice need be proved.
simplified: Facts that are commonly known don't need to be proven.
meaning: Facts judicially noticeable need not be proved

original: The period of limitation for any suit, appeal or application shall be computed from the time when the right to sue accrues.
simplified: Time limit for legal action starts when right to take action arises.

original: Any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere shall be instituted within three years from the date when the right to sue accrues.
simplified: If no specific time limit, lawsuit must be filed within 3 years.
meaning: Any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in this Schedule

original: All non-testamentary documents which purport or operate to create any right, title or interest in immovable property shall be registered.
simplified: Property documents creating rights must be registered.
meaning: Documents of which registration is compulsory

original: No document required by section 17 to be registered shall affect any immovable property unless it has been registered.
simplified: Unregistered property documents cannot affect property rights.
meaning: Effect of non-registration of documents required to be registered

original: A contract of sale of goods is a contract whereby the seller transfers or agrees to transfer the property in goods to the buyer for a price.
simplified: Sale contract means transferring goods ownership to buyer for money.

original: The goods must be of merchantable quality, fit for the purpose for which such goods are commonly bought.
simplified: Goods sold must be of reasonable quality and fit for purpose.
meaning: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness

original: The relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
simplified: Partnership means relationship between persons sharing business profits.

original: Every partner is liable jointly with all the other partners for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner.
simplified: Each partner is personally liable for all partnership debts.
meaning: Liability of a partner for acts of the firm

original: An easement is a right which the owner or occupier of certain land possesses for the beneficial enjoyment of that land.
simplified: Easement is right to use neighbor's land for beneficial enjoyment.

original: The dominant owner is entitled to enjoy the easement without disturbance by any other person.
simplified: Easement holder has right to use easement without interference.

original: A trust is an obligation annexed to the ownership of property, and arising out of a confidence reposed in and accepted by the owner.
simplified: Trust means property ownership with obligation to use for another's benefit.

original: The trustee is bound to fulfil the purpose of the trust, and to obey the directions of the author of the trust.
simplified: Trustee must fulfill trust purpose and follow directions.

original: Every instrument chargeable with duty shall be stamped before or at the time of execution.
simplified: Documents requiring stamp duty must be stamped before signing.

original: No instrument chargeable with duty shall be admitted in evidence unless such instrument is duly stamped.
simplified: Unstamped documents cannot be used as evidence.
meaning: Instruments not duly stamped inadmissible in evidence, etc.

original: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services if that person is a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
simplified: SC/ST community members have right to free legal services.

original: A woman or a child; a person with disability; a person under circumstances of undeserved want are entitled to legal services.
simplified: Women, children, disabled, and needy have right to free legal aid.
meaning: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services

law_type: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
original: A senior citizen including parent who is unable to maintain himself from his own earning shall be entitled to make an application for maintenance.
simplified: Senior citizens unable to support themselves can claim maintenance.
meaning: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens

law_type: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
original: A child or relative shall be liable to maintain a senior citizen if such child or relative neglects or refuses to maintain such senior citizen.
simplified: Children/relatives with means must maintain senior citizens.
meaning: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens

law_type: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
original: No juvenile in conflict with law shall be sentenced to death or imprisonment for any term which may extend to imprisonment for life.
simplified: Juveniles cannot be given death sentence or life imprisonment.
meaning: Order that may be passed regarding juvenile

law_type: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
original: No child shall be subjected to corporal punishment or mental harassment.
simplified: Children cannot be given physical punishment or mental harassment.
meaning: Prohibition on disclosure of identity of children

original: Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge in any process or activity connected with the proceeds of crime shall be guilty of offence of money-laundering.
simplified: Money laundering involves handling illegal money to make it appear legal.

original: Whoever commits the offence of money-laundering shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years.
simplified: Money laundering is punishable with 3+ years rigorous imprisonment.

original: There shall be levied a tax called the goods and services tax on all supplies of goods or services or both.
simplified: GST tax is applied to all sales of goods and services in India.

original: Every registered person shall be entitled to take credit of input tax charged on any supply of goods or services.
simplified: Businesses can claim credit for GST paid on inputs.
meaning: Eligibility and conditions for taking input tax credit

original: Whoever causes the death of a person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Causing death by careless or reckless action is punishable with up to 2 years imprisonment or fine.

original: Whoever, being bound by an oath or by any express provision of law to state the truth, makes any statement which is false, shall be punished.
simplified: Making false statements when legally required to tell truth is punishable.
meaning: False statement on oath or affirmation to public servant

original: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for term which may extend to ten years.
simplified: Giving false evidence in death penalty cases is punishable with life imprisonment or up to 10 years.
meaning: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence

original: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, commits criminal breach of trust.
simplified: Criminal breach of trust involves dishonestly using entrusted property for personal benefit.

original: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Criminal breach of trust is punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both.
meaning: Punishment for criminal breach of trust

original: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property, commits cheating.
simplified: Cheating involves deceiving someone to dishonestly obtain property from them.

original: Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Cheating is punishable with up to 1 year imprisonment or fine or both.

original: Whoever, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person, causes the destruction of any property, commits mischief.
simplified: Mischief involves intentionally causing damage or loss to property.

original: Whoever commits mischief shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Mischief is punishable with up to 3 months imprisonment or fine or both.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept, or attempts to obtain from any person, any gratification whatever, other than legal remuneration, as a motive or reward for doing any official act, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servants taking bribes for official acts can be punished.
meaning: Punishment for public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration

original: When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he has received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit.
simplified: When contract is cancelled, both parties should return any benefits received from the contract.
meaning: Consequences of rescission of voidable contract

original: Where a contract is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it.
simplified: If contract is found void, any benefits received must be returned or compensated.
meaning: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement

original: In the event of breach of contract, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive compensation for any loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach.
simplified: Compensation for contract breach covers losses that naturally result from the breach.
meaning: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract

original: When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default.
simplified: Compensation available even when obligation arises without formal contract.
meaning: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act

original: A contract which is contingent upon the happening of a future uncertain event cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened.
simplified: Contracts depending on uncertain future events can only be enforced after the event happens.
meaning: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening

original: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened.
simplified: Contracts based on 'if something happens' can only be enforced after it actually happens.

original: A contract to do or not to do something, if some event, which is collateral to such contract, does not happen, may be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible.
simplified: Contracts based on 'if something doesn't happen' can be enforced when that event becomes impossible.
meaning: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening

original: Where the consent of the promisor is caused by coercion, the contract is voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
simplified: Contracts made under pressure can be cancelled by the pressured party.
meaning: Voidability of agreements without free consent

original: When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
simplified: Contracts made under excessive influence can be cancelled by the influenced party.
meaning: Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence

original: No female shall be sentenced to death.
simplified: Women cannot be given death sentence.
meaning: Postponement of capital sentence on pregnant woman

original: When any person is sentenced to death, the sentence shall direct that he be hanged by the neck till he is dead.
simplified: Death sentence must specify hanging by neck until death.
meaning: Form and contents of judgment in death sentence cases

original: In the case of any offence punishable with imprisonment for life, the Court may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, impose sentence of imprisonment for a term exceeding ten years.
simplified: Life imprisonment can be given for offenses punishable with life imprisonment, with reasons recorded.
meaning: Sentence in cases of conviction of several offences at one trial

original: No woman shall be called to a police station for questioning.
simplified: Women cannot be called to police station for questioning.
meaning: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses

original: In every inquiry or trial the proceedings shall be held as expeditiously as possible.
simplified: Court proceedings should be completed as quickly as possible.
meaning: Power to postpone or adjourn proceedings

original: Any person accused of an offence before a Criminal Court, or against whom proceedings are instituted under this Code, may of right be defended by a pleader of his choice.
simplified: Every accused person has the right to be defended by a lawyer of their choice.
meaning: Right of person against whom proceedings are instituted to be defended

original: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or, if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, the parties may marry again.
simplified: After divorce becomes final, both parties are free to remarry.
meaning: Divorced persons when may marry again

original: Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding.
simplified: Court can order payment of legal expenses if spouse has no independent income.
meaning: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings

original: When a female Hindu dies intestate, her property shall devolve according to the rules set out in section 16.
simplified: Property of Hindu female without will follows specific inheritance rules.
meaning: General rules of succession in the case of female Hindus

original: Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner.
simplified: Hindu women have full ownership rights over their property, not limited ownership.
meaning: Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property

original: No person shall be capable of being taken in adoption unless he or she is a Hindu, he or she has not already been adopted, he or she has not been married, unless there is a custom or usage applicable to the parties which permits persons who are married being taken in adoption.
simplified: Only unmarried Hindu children can be adopted, unless custom allows married persons adoption.

original: No adoption shall be made after the adoptee has completed the age of fifteen years, unless there is a custom or usage applicable to the parties which permits persons who have completed the age of fifteen years being taken in adoption.
simplified: Adoption generally not allowed after child turns 15, unless custom permits.

original: A Hindu wife shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.
simplified: Hindu wife has right to be maintained by her husband throughout her life.

original: The natural guardians of a Hindu minor, in respect of the minor's person as well as in respect of the minor's property, are the father, and after him, the mother.
simplified: Natural guardians of Hindu minor are: first father, then mother.
meaning: Natural guardians of a Hindu minor

original: The natural guardian of a Hindu minor has power, subject to the provisions of this section, to do all acts which are necessary or reasonable and proper for the benefit of the minor or for the realization, protection or benefit of the minor's estate.
simplified: Natural guardian can take necessary actions for minor's benefit and property protection.

original: A Muslim woman married under Muslim law shall be entitled to obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage on the ground that the husband has neglected or has failed to provide for her maintenance for a period of two years.
simplified: Muslim wife can seek divorce if husband fails to provide maintenance for 2 years.
meaning: Grounds for Muslim woman to seek divorce

original: The dower may be fixed either before or at the time of marriage or after the marriage.
simplified: Mehr (dower) can be decided before, during, or after marriage.
meaning: Provisions regarding dower in Muslim marriage

original: A Muslim husband may dissolve the marriage by pronouncing talaq.
simplified: Muslim husband can divorce by pronouncing talaq.

original: The mother shall be entitled to the custody of her minor child up to the age of seven years in the case of a boy and upto the age of puberty in the case of a girl.
simplified: Mother has custody rights: for son until age 7, for daughter until puberty.

original: A Muslim is entitled to bequeath by will only one-third of his property.
simplified: Muslim can will only one-third of property, rest follows inheritance rules.

original: Any marriage celebrated, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the petition of either the husband or the wife on the ground that the other party has, after the solemnization of the marriage, had voluntary sexual intercourse with any person other than his or her spouse.
simplified: Marriage under Special Marriage Act can be dissolved if either spouse has extramarital affair.
meaning: Grounds for divorce under Special Marriage Act

original: Any marriage under this Act may be solemnized in any form which the parties may choose to adopt.
simplified: Marriages under this Act can be performed in any form chosen by the parties.

original: When a marriage has been dissolved and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, either party to the marriage may marry again.
simplified: After divorce becomes final under this Act, parties can remarry.
meaning: Divorced persons when may marry again

original: Whoever commits an offence under section 138 shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
simplified: Cheque bouncing is punishable with up to 2 years imprisonment or double the cheque amount as fine or both.

original: A promissory note is an instrument in writing containing an unconditional undertaking, signed by the maker, to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person, or to the bearer of the instrument.
simplified: Promissory note is a written promise to pay specific amount to specific person or bearer.

original: A bill of exchange is an instrument in writing containing an unconditional order, signed by the maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person or to the bearer of the instrument.
simplified: Bill of exchange is a written order to pay specific amount to specific person or bearer.

original: A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand.
simplified: Cheque is a type of bill of exchange payable on demand from a bank.

original: The District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed one crore rupees.
simplified: District consumer court can hear cases involving claims up to ₹1 crore.

original: The State Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds one crore rupees but does not exceed ten crore rupees.
simplified: State consumer court can hear cases involving claims between ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore.

original: The National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds ten crore rupees.
simplified: National consumer court can hear cases involving claims over ₹10 crore.

original: An information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or would be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record in question.
simplified: Information should be provided in requested format unless it would harm records or require excessive resources.

original: Where a decision is taken to provide the information on payment of any further fee representing the cost of providing the information, the Central Public Information Officer shall send an intimation to the person making the request.
simplified: If additional fees are required for providing information, applicant must be informed about the details.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, there shall be no obligation to give any citizen information which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India.
simplified: Certain sensitive information affecting national security and interests can be withheld.

original: Whoever commits hacking shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both.
simplified: Hacking is punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment or ₹5 lakh fine or both.

original: Whoever sends by means of a computer resource any information that is grossly offensive or has menacing character shall be punishable.
simplified: Sending offensive or false information through computers is punishable.
meaning: Punishment for sending offensive messages through communication service

original: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished.
simplified: Taking or sharing private images without consent violating privacy is punishable.

original: Whoever, knowingly or intentionally conceals, destroys or alters any computer source code used for a computer resource with an intention to cause damage, shall be punishable.
simplified: Destroying or altering computer source code with intent to cause damage is punishable.

original: Every company shall prepare its financial statements in accordance with the accounting standards.
simplified: Companies must prepare financial statements following accounting standards.

original: The Board of Directors of every company shall consist of individuals as directors and shall have a minimum number of three directors in the case of a public company, two directors in the case of a private company.
simplified: Minimum directors required: Public company-3, Private company-2, One Person Company-1.
meaning: Company to have Board of Directors

original: No company shall appoint or re-appoint any person as its managing director, whole-time director or manager for a term exceeding five years at a time.
simplified: Managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed for more than 5 years at once.
meaning: Appointment of managing director, whole-time director or manager

original: Every company having a paid-up share capital of five crore rupees or more shall constitute a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee of the Board.
simplified: Companies with ₹5 crore+ paid-up capital must have CSR committee.

original: The Board of every company shall ensure that the company spends, in every financial year, at least two per cent of the average net profits of the company made during the three immediately preceding financial years.
simplified: Companies must spend at least 2% of average net profits of last 3 years on CSR activities.

original: The input tax credit shall be availed by a registered person on the basis of any of the following documents, namely: an invoice issued by the supplier of goods or services or both.
simplified: Input tax credit can be claimed based on invoices from suppliers.
meaning: Documents for claiming input tax credit

original: Every registered person required to deduct tax at source under section 51 shall furnish a return in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
simplified: Persons required to deduct TDS must file returns in prescribed format.

original: Any registered person who fails to furnish the details of outward or inward supplies required under section 37 by the due date shall be liable to pay a late fee of one hundred rupees for every day.
simplified: Late filing of supply details attracts ₹100 per day late fee.
meaning: Levy of late fee for delayed filing of return

original: The arbitral tribunal shall make an arbitral award within a period of twelve months from the date the arbitral tribunal enters upon the reference.
simplified: Arbitration award should be made within 12 months from when tribunal starts proceedings.

original: An arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively.
simplified: Arbitration award is final and legally binding on all parties involved.

original: Recourse to a Court against an arbitral award may be made only by an application for setting aside such award in accordance with sub-section (2) and sub-section (3).
simplified: Court can only interfere with arbitration award through specific setting aside procedure.
meaning: Application for setting aside arbitral award

original: Sale is a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised.
simplified: Sale means transferring property ownership for money paid or promised.

original: Gift is the transfer of certain existing movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and accepted by or on behalf of the donee.
simplified: Gift means transferring property voluntarily without payment, from donor to donee.

original: An exchange is a mutual transfer of ownership of one thing for the ownership of another.
simplified: Exchange means swapping ownership of one property for another property.

original: Facts which, though not in issue, are so connected with a fact in issue as to form part of the same transaction, are relevant, whether they occurred at the same time and place or at different times and places.
simplified: Facts connected to the main issue as part of same transaction are relevant evidence.
meaning: Relevancy of facts forming part of same transaction

original: Any fact which enables the court to determine the amount of damages which ought to be awarded is relevant.
simplified: Facts that help determine compensation amount are relevant evidence.

original: When one person has, by his declaration, act or omission, intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed to deny the truth of that thing.
simplified: If someone makes another believe something is true and they act on it, the first person cannot later deny it.

original: No witness who is not a party to a suit shall be compelled to produce his title-deeds to any property.
simplified: Witnesses cannot be forced to produce documents that might incriminate them or reveal property titles.
meaning: Production of documents which another person, having possession, could refuse to produce

original: The Court may, either on its own motion or on the application of any party, order any fact to be proved by affidavit.
simplified: Court can allow facts to be proved through written statements (affidavits).
meaning: Power to order any point to be proved by affidavit

original: No second appeal shall lie except on the grounds of substantial question of law.
simplified: Second appeal to High Court only allowed for important legal questions, not factual disputes.

original: The Court may, if it thinks fit, make an order for security for costs at any stage of the suit.
simplified: Court can order plaintiff to deposit security money for defendant's legal costs.
meaning: Power to order security for costs

original: No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place, and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place, unless the vehicle is covered by a policy of insurance.
simplified: All vehicles must have valid insurance before being driven on public roads.
meaning: Necessity for insurance against third party risks

original: Whoever drives a motor vehicle in any public place without holding an effective policy of insurance shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
simplified: Driving without insurance can lead to 3 months imprisonment or ₹1000 fine or both.

original: Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances of the case, shall be punishable.
simplified: Dangerous driving is punishable under the Act.

original: Where any offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was directly in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence.
simplified: Company officials can be held personally liable for environmental offenses committed by company.

law_type: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
original: No person shall knowingly cause or permit any poisonous, noxious or polluting matter determined in accordance with such standards as may be laid down by the State Board to enter into any stream or well or sewer or on land.
simplified: No one can knowingly allow pollutants to enter water bodies beyond prescribed standards.

law_type: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
original: No person operating any industrial plant shall discharge or cause or permit to be discharged the emission of any air pollutant in excess of the standards laid down by the State Board.
simplified: Industries cannot release air pollutants beyond prescribed standards.
meaning: Restrictions on emission of air pollutants

original: No person shall hunt any wild animal specified in Schedules I, II, III and IV except as provided under section 11 and section 12.
simplified: Hunting protected wild animals is prohibited except under specific permissions.
meaning: Prohibition of hunting of wild animals

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force in a State, no State Government shall make, except with the prior approval of the Central Government, any order directing that any forest land may be used for any non-forest purpose.
simplified: Forest land cannot be used for non-forest purposes without central government approval.
meaning: Restriction on the dereservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purpose

original: Whoever commits the offence of criminal misconduct shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than four years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Criminal misconduct by public servant is punishable with 4-10 years imprisonment and fine.
meaning: Criminal misconduct by a public servant

original: Whoever commits the offence of money-laundering shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Money laundering is punishable with 3-7 years rigorous imprisonment and fine.

law_type: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
original: Whoever commits sexual harassment upon a child shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Sexual harassment of child is punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.

law_type: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
original: The evidence of the child shall be recorded within a period of thirty days of the special court taking cognizance of the offence.
simplified: Child's evidence must be recorded within 30 days of court taking case.
meaning: Procedure for recording evidence of child

law_type: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
original: No juvenile in conflict with law shall be sentenced to death or imprisonment for any term which may extend to imprisonment for life.
simplified: Juveniles cannot be given death sentence or life imprisonment.
meaning: Prohibition of certain punishments for juvenile in conflict with law

law_type: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
original: No child shall be subjected to corporal punishment or mental harassment.
simplified: Children cannot be given physical punishment or mental harassment.

law_type: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
original: A senior citizen including parent who is unable to maintain himself from his own earning or out of the property owned by him, shall be entitled to make an application for maintenance.
simplified: Senior citizens and parents unable to support themselves can claim maintenance from children/relatives.
meaning: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens

law_type: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
original: A child or relative, as the case may be, shall be liable to maintain a senior citizen including parent, if such child or relative, being possessed of sufficient means, neglects or refuses to maintain such senior citizen.
simplified: Children/relatives with sufficient means must maintain senior citizens/parents who cannot support themselves.
meaning: Obligation of children to maintain parents

original: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services under this Act if that person is a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
simplified: SC/ST community members have right to free legal services for court cases.

original: A woman or a child; a person with disability; a person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; or an industrial workman; or in custody, are entitled to legal services.
simplified: Women, children, disabled, disaster victims, workers, and persons in custody have right to free legal aid.

original: Any person suing for the specific performance of a contract may also ask for compensation for its breach, either in addition to, or in substitution of, such performance.
simplified: Person seeking contract enforcement can also claim compensation for breach.
meaning: Power to award compensation in certain cases

original: Temporary injunctions are such as are to continue until a specified time, or until the further order of the court.
simplified: Temporary injunctions last for specified time or until court orders otherwise.

original: The period of limitation for a suit to recover possession of immovable property is twelve years from the date when the possession of the defendant becomes adverse to the plaintiff.
simplified: Property possession recovery lawsuit must be filed within 12 years from when adverse possession started.
meaning: Suit for possession of immovable property

original: All non-testamentary documents which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish, whether in present or in future, any right, title or interest, whether vested or contingent, of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, to or in immovable property, shall be registered.
simplified: Property documents creating rights worth ₹100+ must be registered.
meaning: Documents of which registration is compulsory

original: Every instrument chargeable with duty shall be stamped before or at the time of execution.
simplified: Documents requiring stamp duty must be stamped before or when signed.

original: No instrument chargeable with duty shall be admitted in evidence for any purpose by any person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence, unless such instrument is duly stamped.
simplified: Unstamped documents cannot be used as evidence in legal proceedings.
meaning: Instruments not duly stamped inadmissible in evidence

original: A partner may retire with the consent of all the other partners, or in accordance with an express agreement by the partners, or where the partnership is at will, by giving notice in writing to all the other partners of his intention to retire.
simplified: Partner can retire with consent of all partners, as per agreement, or by notice in partnership at will.

original: Where there is a contract for the sale of unascertained goods, no property in the goods is transferred to the buyer unless and until the goods are ascertained.
simplified: For unspecified goods, ownership transfers only when specific goods are identified.

original: An easement is a right which the owner or occupier of certain land possesses, as such, for the beneficial enjoyment of that land, to do and continue to do something, or to prevent and continue to prevent something being done, in or upon, or in respect of, certain other land not his own.
simplified: Easement is right to use neighbor's land for beneficial enjoyment of one's own land.

original: A trust is an obligation annexed to the ownership of property, and arising out of a confidence reposed in and accepted by the owner, or declared and accepted by him, for the benefit of another, or of another and the owner.
simplified: Trust means property ownership with obligation to use it for another's benefit.

original: Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall be punished.
simplified: Attempting to commit serious crimes is itself a punishable offense.
meaning: Punishment for attempting to commit offences

original: Whoever, being bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.
simplified: Giving false statement when legally required to tell truth is giving false evidence.

original: Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by the law for the time being in force in India, shall be punished with imprisonment for life.
simplified: Giving false evidence in death penalty cases is punishable with life imprisonment.
meaning: Giving false evidence in capital cases

original: Whoever uses any false evidence knowing the same to be false, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave or fabricated false evidence.
simplified: Using false evidence knowingly is as punishable as creating false evidence.
meaning: Using evidence known to be false

original: Whoever issues or signs any certificate required by law to be given or signed, or relating to any fact of which such certificate is by law admissible in evidence, knowing or believing that such certificate is false in any material point, shall be punished.
simplified: Issuing false certificates is punishable like giving false evidence.

original: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, causes any evidence of the commission of that offence to disappear, with the intention of screening the offender from legal punishment, shall be punished.
simplified: Hiding evidence to protect offender from punishment is a crime.

original: Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, gives any information respecting that offence which he knows or believes to be false, shall be punished.
simplified: Giving false information about a crime is punishable.
meaning: Giving false information respecting an offence

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being, as such public servant, charged with the preparation or translation of any document, frames or translates that document in a manner which he knows or believes to be incorrect, intending thereby to cause injury to any person, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant preparing incorrect documents to harm someone is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces in any stage of a judicial proceeding any report, order, verdict, or decision which he knows to be contrary to law, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant giving illegal judgments or orders corruptly is punishable.
meaning: Public servant making report contrary to law

original: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
simplified: Causing simple injury is punishable with up to 1 year imprisonment or ₹1000 fine.

original: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Causing serious injury is punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.
meaning: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt

original: Whoever voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished.
simplified: Causing injury with dangerous weapons is punishable.
meaning: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons

original: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simplified: Kidnapping is punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

original: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman to compel her marriage, or for any other unlawful purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years.
simplified: Kidnapping woman for marriage is punishable with up to 10 years imprisonment.

original: Whoever imports, exports, removes, buys, sells or disposes of any person as a slave, or accepts, receives or detains against his will any person as a slave, shall be punished.
simplified: Slavery and slave trade are punishable offenses.
meaning: Buying or disposing of any person as a slave

original: Whoever, by means of criminal intimidation, commits extortion, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simplified: Extortion through threats is punishable with up to 2 years imprisonment.
meaning: Extortion by threat of accusation of an offence punishable with death

original: Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending to cause injury to any person, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant knowingly disobeying legal directions is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant allowing document removal from custody is punishable.
meaning: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant negligently allowing document removal is punishable.
meaning: Public servant negligently suffering such escape

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant allowing prisoner escape is punishable.
meaning: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner to escape

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant negligently allowing prisoner escape is punishable.
meaning: Public servant negligently suffering prisoner to escape

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant aiding prisoner escape is punishable.
meaning: Public servant aiding escape of prisoner

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant harboring escaped prisoner is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant omitting to apprehend escaped prisoner is punishable.
meaning: Public servant omitting to apprehend escaped prisoner

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant omitting to assist in apprehending escaped prisoner is punishable.
meaning: Public servant omitting to assist in apprehending escaped prisoner

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant resisting lawful apprehension is punishable.
meaning: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant escaping from lawful custody is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant rescuing from lawful custody is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant harbouring offender is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant taking gift to screen offender is punishable.
meaning: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant offering gift to screen offender is punishable.
meaning: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant taking gift to help recover stolen property is punishable.
meaning: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant harbouring robber or dacoit is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant harbouring offender of capital offence is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant omitting to apprehend or suffer escape of person charged with capital offence is punishable.
meaning: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant negligently suffering escape of person charged with capital offence is punishable.
meaning: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend persons under sentence or lawfully committed

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant escaping from custody or omitting to apprehend is punishable.
meaning: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant resisting or obstructing lawful apprehension is punishable.
meaning: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant intentionally omitting to apprehend is punishable.
meaning: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant negligently suffering escape is punishable.
meaning: Negligent suffering of escape from confinement or custody

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant resisting or obstructing lawful apprehension is punishable.
meaning: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant escaping from lawful custody is punishable.

original: Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the custody of any document, voluntarily allows any person to take away or secrete that document, shall be punished.
simplified: Public servant rescuing from lawful custody is punishable.

original: When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he has received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit.
simplified: When contract is cancelled, both parties should return any benefits received from the contract.
meaning: Consequences of rescission of voidable contract

original: Where a contract is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it.
simplified: If contract is found void, any benefits received must be returned or compensated.
meaning: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement

original: In the event of breach of contract, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive compensation for any loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach.
simplified: Compensation for contract breach covers losses that naturally result from the breach.
meaning: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract

original: When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default.
simplified: Compensation available even when obligation arises without formal contract.
meaning: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act

original: A contract which is contingent upon the happening of a future uncertain event cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened.
simplified: Contracts depending on uncertain future events can only be enforced after the event happens.
meaning: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening

original: Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened.
simplified: Contracts based on 'if something happens' can only be enforced after it actually happens.

original: A contract to do or not to do something, if some event, which is collateral to such contract, does not happen, may be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible.
simplified: Contracts based on 'if something doesn't happen' can be enforced when that event becomes impossible.
meaning: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening

original: Where the consent of the promisor is caused by coercion, the contract is voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
simplified: Contracts made under pressure can be cancelled by the pressured party.
meaning: Voidability of agreements without free consent

original: When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
simplified: Contracts made under excessive influence can be cancelled by the influenced party.
meaning: Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence

original: No female shall be sentenced to death.
simplified: Women cannot be given death sentence.
meaning: Postponement of capital sentence on pregnant woman

original: When any person is sentenced to death, the sentence shall direct that he be hanged by the neck till he is dead.
simplified: Death sentence must specify hanging by neck until death.
meaning: Form and contents of judgment in death sentence cases

original: In the case of any offence punishable with imprisonment for life, the Court may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, impose sentence of imprisonment for a term exceeding ten years.
simplified: Life imprisonment can be given for offenses punishable with life imprisonment, with reasons recorded.
meaning: Sentence in cases of conviction of several offences at one trial

original: No woman shall be called to a police station for questioning.
simplified: Women cannot be called to police station for questioning.
meaning: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses

original: In every inquiry or trial the proceedings shall be held as expeditiously as possible.
simplified: Court proceedings should be completed as quickly as possible.
meaning: Power to postpone or adjourn proceedings

original: Any person accused of an offence before a Criminal Court, or against whom proceedings are instituted under this Code, may of right be defended by a pleader of his choice.
simplified: Every accused person has the right to be defended by a lawyer of their choice.
meaning: Right of person against whom proceedings are instituted to be defended

original: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or, if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, the parties may marry again.
simplified: After divorce becomes final, both parties are free to remarry.
meaning: Divorced persons when may marry again

original: Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding.
simplified: Court can order payment of legal expenses if spouse has no independent income.
meaning: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings

original: When a female Hindu dies intestate, her property shall devolve according to the rules set out in section 16.
simplified: Property of Hindu female without will follows specific inheritance rules.
meaning: General rules of succession in the case of female Hindus

original: Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner.
simplified: Hindu women have full ownership rights over their property, not limited ownership.
meaning: Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property

original: No person shall be capable of being taken in adoption unless he or she is a Hindu, he or she has not already been adopted, he or she has not been married, unless there is a custom or usage applicable to the parties which permits persons who are married being taken in adoption.
simplified: Only unmarried Hindu children can be adopted, unless custom allows married persons adoption.

original: No adoption shall be made after the adoptee has completed the age of fifteen years, unless there is a custom or usage applicable to the parties which permits persons who have completed the age of fifteen years being taken in adoption.
simplified: Adoption generally not allowed after child turns 15, unless custom permits.

original: A Hindu wife shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.
simplified: Hindu wife has right to be maintained by her husband throughout her life.

original: The natural guardians of a Hindu minor, in respect of the minor's person as well as in respect of the minor's property, are the father, and after him, the mother.
simplified: Natural guardians of Hindu minor are: first father, then mother.
meaning: Natural guardians of a Hindu minor

original: The natural guardian of a Hindu minor has power, subject to the provisions of this section, to do all acts which are necessary or reasonable and proper for the benefit of the minor or for the realization, protection or benefit of the minor's estate.
simplified: Natural guardian can take necessary actions for minor's benefit and property protection.

original: A Muslim woman married under Muslim law shall be entitled to obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage on the ground that the husband has neglected or has failed to provide for her maintenance for a period of two years.
simplified: Muslim wife can seek divorce if husband fails to provide maintenance for 2 years.
meaning: Grounds for Muslim woman to seek divorce

original: The dower may be fixed either before or at the time of marriage or after the marriage.
simplified: Mehr (dower) can be decided before, during, or after marriage.
meaning: Provisions regarding dower in Muslim marriage

original: A Muslim husband may dissolve the marriage by pronouncing talaq.
simplified: Muslim husband can divorce by pronouncing talaq.

original: The mother shall be entitled to the custody of her minor child up to the age of seven years in the case of a boy and upto the age of puberty in the case of a girl.
simplified: Mother has custody rights: for son until age 7, for daughter until puberty.

original: A Muslim is entitled to bequeath by will only one-third of his property.
simplified: Muslim can will only one-third of property, rest follows inheritance rules.

original: Any marriage celebrated, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the petition of either the husband or the wife on the ground that the other party has, after the solemnization of the marriage, had voluntary sexual intercourse with any person other than his or her spouse.
simplified: Marriage under Special Marriage Act can be dissolved if either spouse has extramarital affair.
meaning: Grounds for divorce under Special Marriage Act

original: Any marriage under this Act may be solemnized in any form which the parties may choose to adopt.
simplified: Marriages under this Act can be performed in any form chosen by the parties.

original: When a marriage has been dissolved and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, either party to the marriage may marry again.
simplified: After divorce becomes final under this Act, parties can remarry.
meaning: Divorced persons when may marry again
